;; Paths under these prefixes skip "file changed" / "Reread from disk?" (something on the mount triggers false positives).
(defvar my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes '("/home/gmare/mount/")
  "List of path prefixes (strings). For files under these, never prompt 'file changed' / 'Reread from disk?'.
Customize if your mount is elsewhere, e.g. (setq my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes '(\"/mnt/nfs\"))")
(defun my-file-under-skip-change-check-p (filename)
  (and filename
       (boundp 'my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes)
       my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes
       (let ((expanded (expand-file-name filename)))
         (cl-some (lambda (prefix) (string-prefix-p (expand-file-name prefix) expanded))
                  my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes))))
;; "File changed on disk. Reread?" — skip for paths in my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes; else default (timestamp).
(advice-add 'ask-user-about-supersession-threat :around
            (lambda (orig fn)
              (if (my-file-under-skip-change-check-p fn)
                  nil
                  (funcall orig fn)))
            '((name . my-supersession-skip-mount-paths)))
;; "Save anyway?" — skip for paths in my-skip-file-changed-check-prefixes; else use normal timestamp check.
(advice-add 'verify-visited-file-modtime :around
            (lambda (orig &rest args)
              (if (my-file-under-skip-change-check-p (buffer-file-name))
                  nil
                  (apply orig args)))
            '((name . my-verify-modtime-skip-mount-paths)))

      "Return list of available model names from Ollama /api/tags."
      (let ((buf (url-retrieve-synchronously
                  (concat my-ollama-url "/api/tags") t nil 3)))
	(when (buffer-live-p buf)
          (with-current-buffer buf
            (goto-char (point-min))
            (prog1
		(when (re-search-forward "^\r?$" nil t)
                  (condition-case nil
                      (let ((data (json-read)))
			(mapcar (lambda (m) (alist-get 'name m))
				(alist-get 'models data)))
                    (error nil)))
              (kill-buffer buf))))))

(defun my-ellama-refresh-providers ()
  "Update `ellama-providers' from Ollama model list.
  Returns the new alist, or nil if Ollama unreachable."
  (interactive)
  (let ((models (my-ollama-list-models))
        (providers))
    (when models
      (dolist (m models)
        (unless (string-match-p "\\`nomic-embed\\|embed\\|all-minilm" m)
          (push (cons m
                      (make-llm-ollama
                       :chat-model m
                       :embedding-model "nomic-embed-text"
                       :default-chat-non-standard-params '(("num_ctx" . 32768))))
                providers)))
      (setq providers (nreverse providers))
      (setopt ellama-providers providers)
      (message "ellama: %d models loaded from %s" (length providers) my-ollama-url)
      providers)))

(defun gptel-load-and-call ()
  "Load gptel, backends, and gptel_tools on first use; then run gptel."
  (interactive)
  (unless (featurep 'gptel)
    (use-package mcp)
    (use-package gptel)

    (use-package gptel-agent)
    ;; (use-package gptel-org)
    (defvar gptel-jetson-backend
      (gptel-make-ollama "Jetson"
        ;;:host "ollama.jetson/mcp"
        :host "bottino/mcp"
        :protocol "http"
        :stream nil
        :curl-args '("-k" "--connect-timeout" "15" "--max-time" "120")
        :request-params '(:options (:num_gpu 20))
        :models '(qwen2.5-coder:3b qwen3.5:9b llama3.2:latest codegemma:7b deepseek-coder:6.7b gemma4:latest dolphin-mistral)))

          gptel-include-tool-results 'auto)

(defun elmo-python-code ()
  "Function to integrate ELMo-like functionality using Python."
  (interactive)
  ;; Assuming you have a Python script that interacts with ELMo and
  returns results.
  (let ((python-eldoc-buffer (make-temp-file "elmocode" nil t)))
    (with-current-buffer python-eldoc-buffer
      (insert "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n"
              "import json\n"
              "\n"
              "def elmo_functionality(text):\n"
              f"   # Dummy ELMo function that returns a JSON
              object. Replace with actual ELMo call.\n"
              f"   return {json.dumps({'result': 'processed
              text'})}\n"
              "\n"
              "result = elmo_functionality('"'"'Your input text
              here'"'"')\n")
      (write-region nil nil python-eldoc-buffer)
      (shell-command (concat "chmod +x " python-eldoc-buffer))
      (call-process-shell-command
       python-eldoc-buffer
       :stderr nil
       :read-only t
       :treat-piped-output-as-errors nil))

    ;; Now you can access the result in your current buffer.
    (message "ELMo function call completed. Result is accessible via `M-x elmo-python-code`")
    ))

(defun my/ollama-chat (prompt)
  "Send PROMPT to Ollama and show the response in a temp buffer."
  (interactive "sPrompt: ")
  (let* ((url-request-method "POST")
         (url-request-extra-headers
          '(("Content-Type" . "application/json")))
         (url-request-data
          (encode-coding-string
           (json-encode
            `(("model" . "llama3.2")
              ("stream" . :json-false)
              ("prompt" . ,prompt)))
           'utf-8))
         (buf (url-retrieve-synchronously "http://localhost:11434/api/generate")))
    (with-current-buffer buf
      (goto-char (point-min))
      (re-search-forward "^$")
      (forward-char 1)
      (let ((json-object-type 'alist))
        (message "%s" (alist-get 'response (json-read)))))
    (kill-buffer buf)))

services:

:GPTEL_BACKEND: Jetson
This project make use of nvidia jetson capabilities using it as a central hub for an embedded cluster.
*** nvidia jetson capabilities
NVIDIA Jetson is a series of single-board computers designed by NVIDIA, specifically optimized for edge computing and machine learning applications. It consists of a dedicated processor that can perform computations much faster than traditional x86-based PCs.
Here are some key features and capabilities of NVIDIA Jetson:
1. *Hardware Architecture*: Jetson devices feature the Tegra SoC (System on Chip), which is a powerful 64-bit ARM architecture with integrated high-performance GPUs. This combination allows for efficient processing power, high image resolution, and real-time computations.
2. *GPU Acceleration*: The Jetson GPUs are designed to support CUDA programming, enabling developers to perform parallel computing tasks efficiently. They can handle complex machine learning models, deep neural networks, and other computationally intensive applications at a lower power consumption compared to traditional desktop GPUs.
3. *Power Efficiency*: Designed for low-power consumption and heat dissipation, Jetson devices can operate in environments with limited resources, making them ideal for edge computing applications such as IoT (Internet of Things) nodes, autonomous vehicles, and embedded systems.
4. *Deep Learning Support*: With TensorFlow Lite, CUDA, cuDNN, and other libraries, Jetson provides extensive support for deep learning and machine learning models. This allows developers to deploy complex AI models on the device itself, reducing latency and bandwidth requirements compared to cloud-based solutions.
5. *Modular Design*: Jetson devices can be customized with various expansion boards that allow users to add hardware accelerators like GPUs, cameras, and sensors. This flexibility enables a wide range of applications across different industries.
6. *Open Source Software*: NVIDIA provides open-source software and SDKs for developers to leverage the power of Jetson devices. This includes CUDA Toolkit, cuDNN libraries, and other tools that facilitate development and deployment.
7. *Developer Support*: NVIDIA offers extensive documentation, forums, and tutorials to help developers get started with Jetson and develop custom applications.
8. *Wide Range of Applications*: Jetson is used in various industries, including autonomous driving, healthcare, retail, transportation, and more, where real-time processing and high accuracy are critical.
Overall, Jetson devices provide a powerful platform for edge computing, enabling developers to build intelligent systems that operate efficiently and at scale on small, low-power devices.

# Troubleshooting - LLM Inference on Acer Nitro V 16 AI AMD

## Common Issues & Solutions

### Issue 1: CUDA Out of Memory (OOM)

**Symptoms**:
```
Error: CUDA out of memory - allocate less
```

**Cause**: Model exceeds 8GB VRAM
**Solutions**:
1. Use quantization: `ollama run llama3:8b --quantize int4`
2. Offload layers: `OLLM_NUM_GPU=8`
3. Use RAM fallback (if available)
4. Use smaller model: Llama 3 (3B)

### Issue 2: Model Loading Slow

**Symptoms**:
- Takes >5 minutes to load model
- High RAM usage during load

**Cause**: Loading from disk without preload
**Solutions**:
1. Enable preload: `OLLAMA_LOAD_CPU=10`
2. Use quantized models (smaller)
3. Increase batch size
4. Reduce `OLLAMA_NUM_THREAD`

### Issue 3: Poor Tokens/sec Performance

**Symptoms**:
- <10 tokens/sec on 7B model
- High latency per token

**Cause**:
- Memory paging to RAM
- Background processes
- Suboptimal quantization

**Solutions**:
1. Use int4 quantization
2. Enable MLOCK: `OLLAMA_MLOCK=1`
3. Close background apps
4. Ensure sufficient free RAM

### Issue 4: GPU Utilization Low

**Symptoms**:
- <40% GPU utilization
- System feels slow

**Cause**:
- Inference on CPU instead of GPU
- No model loaded
- Model too large for GPU

**Solutions**:
1. Check: `nvidia-smi`
2. Ensure model loaded to VRAM
3. Reduce model size
4. Check CUDA drivers

### Issue 5: High CPU Usage on 260/7

**Symptoms**:
- CPU temps > 85C
- Background processes high

**Cause**:
- Token generation on CPU
- Pre/post processing overhead
- Batch processing on CPU

**Solutions**:
1. Use GPU for token generation
2. Reduce batch size
3. Close unnecessary apps
4. Limit e-Cores

### Issue 6: NPU Not Available

**Symptoms**:
- `OLLAMA_NPU` returns error
- No Xilinx RF device

**Cause**:
- Hardware doesn't include NPU
- Driver not installed
- NPU hardware absent

**Solutions**:
1. Use GPU only
2. Remove `OLLAMA_NPU=true`
3. Focus on RTX 5060 optimization

## Monitoring Commands

### Check GPU Status
```bash
nvidia-smi
```

### Check Memory Usage
```bash
watch -n 1 'free -h'
```

### Check VRAM Usage
```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
```

### Check Process Memory
```bash
ps aux | grep ollama | grep python
```

### Monitor GPU Temperature
```bash
watch -n 1 'nvidia-smi | grep Temp'
```

### Check CUDA Version
```bash
nvidia-smi | grep CUDA
```

## Prevention Checklist

Before running LLM:
- [ ] VRAM usage < 7GB
- [ ] Model quantized to int4
- [ ] MLOCK enabled
- [ ] No browser tabs running
- [ ] Background apps closed

After loading models:
- [ ] No memory leaks detected
- [ ] Tokens/sec stable
- [ ] GPU temp < 70C
- [ ] No swap usage

## Performance Optimization

### Before First Run
```bash
# Set environment
export OLLAMA_NUM_GPU=1
export OLLAMA_MLOCK=1
export OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_F16=true
export OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM=8151
export OLLAMA_USE_NVIDIA=true
```

### Model Selection
```bash
# Quantize to int4
ollama run llama3:8b:q4_K_M

# Small model for fast loading
ollama run llama3:3b-q4_K_M
```

### Multi-Model Setup
```bash
# Load small models
ollama list
ollama run llama3:3b
ollama run qwen2.5:7b

# Check VRAM usage
nvidia-smi
```

## Hardware Limitations

| Limitation | Workaround |
|---|---|
| Single GPU (8GB VRAM) | Use quantization |
| No NPU | Use GPU/VRAM instead |
| 30GB RAM (DDR5) | Enable RAM fallback |
| 8-core CPU | Limit background tasks |

## Getting Help

1. Check this documentation first
2. Review performance benchmarks
3. Check environment variables
4. Monitor GPU/VRAM usage

EOF

Run these commands to verify laptop specs:

```bash
# GPU
nvidia-smi
lspci -n | grep VGA

nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.current.sm --format=csv

if [ -d /dev/npu0 ]; then echo "NPU device available"; fi
```

from manim import *

class IntroScene(Scene):
    """Simple introduction scene for Blender Twin presentation."""
    
    def construct(self):
        # Create title text
        title = Text("Blender Twin IoT Project", font_size=48)
        
        # Animate title in
        self.play(Write(title))
        
        # Add subtitle
        subtitle = Text("Real-time sensor data integration", font_size=32)
        subtitle.to_edge(DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(subtitle))
        
        # Wait for viewer to read

"""
Blender Twin IoT Animation Scenes
=================================
Manim animation scripts for IoT presentation.
"""

from manim import *

# Global color palette
SENSOR_COLOR = BLUE
BATTERY_COLOR = RED

# =============================================================================
# Intro
# =============================================================================


class IntroScene(Scene):
    """Simple introduction scene for Blender Twin presentation."""
    def construct(self):
        title = Text("Blender Twin IoT Project", font_size=48)
        subtitle = Text("Real-time sensor data integration", font_size=32)
        
        subtitle.to_edge(DOWN)
        self.play(Create(title))
        self.play(Create(subtitle))
        
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))


# =============================================================================
# Sensor Network
# =============================================================================


class SensorNetworkScene(Scene):
    """Visualize Bluetooth mesh network with multiple sensor nodes."""
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        sensor_count = 6
        node_spacing = 2
        mesh_radius = 3  # meters
        # Create scene background
        background = Square(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.0)
        # Position sensor nodes around center
        node_positions = np.array([
            [0, 0, 0],      # Central gateway
            [mesh_radius, 0, 0],
            [-mesh_radius, 0, 0],
            [0, mesh_radius, 0],
            [0, -mesh_radius, 0],
            [0, 0, mesh_radius],
        ])
        # Create sensor nodes with labels
        sensor_labels = [
            "Gateway",
            "Daisy Seed",  # Temperature
            "Axoloti",     # Audio/Sound
            "Xiao",        # BLE Mesh
            "Xiao",        # BLE Mesh
            "daisy_seed",  # I2S/Touch
        ]
        
        for i in range(sensor_count):
            label = Text(sensor_labels[i], font_size=20)
            label_node = label.next_to(
                Circle().scale(0.5),
                DL,
                buff=0.3
            )
            
            # Animate node creation
            self.play(
                Create(label_node),
                FadeIn(Dot(
                    point=node_positions[i], 
                    radius=0.03,
                    color=YELLOW
                ))
            )
        # Create BLE connection lines
        self.play(
            Create(DashedLine(
                start=ORIGIN,
                end_point=[mesh_radius, 0, 0],
                color=BLUE,
            ))
        )
        # Add mesh connection legend
        legend = VGroup(
            Tex("BLE Mesh", font_size=20),
            SolidStroke(DashedLine(color=BLUE)).scale(0.3),
        )
        legend_arr = VGroup(legend)
        legend_arr.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).to_corner(DR)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(legend_arr), Write(legend_arr))
        
        # Complete animation
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(background))


# =============================================================================
# MQTT Flow
# =============================================================================


class MQTTFlowScene(Scene):
    """Demonstrate MQTT publish/subscribe architecture."""

    def construct(self):
        # Create MQTT broker central node
        broker = Text("MQTT Broker", font_size=48)
        broker.to_edge(UP)
        
        # Create topic branches
        topics = VGroup(
            Text("axoloti/audio", font_size=30),
            Text("daisy/sensor", font_size=30),
            Text("xiao/bat", font_size=30),
        )
        
        # Position topics
        topics[0].align_to(topics[0], LEFT)
        topics[1].align_to(topics[0], LEFT)
        topics[2].align_to(topics[0], LEFT)
        
        self.play(
            Write(broker),
            Create(topics[0]),
            Create(topics[1]),
            Create(topics[2]),
            lag_ratio=0.1
        )
        
        # Create subscription arrows
        arrows = VGroup(
            Arrow(broker, topics[0], color=GREEN, buff=0.05),
            Arrow(broker, topics[1], color=GREEN, buff=0.05),
            Arrow(broker, topics[2], color=GREEN, buff=0.05),
        )
        
        # Simulate message flow
        message = Text(
            "Publish: temperature=25.3°C",
            font_size=24, 
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        # Publish animation
        broker_circle = Circle(color=BLUE, radius=0.3)
        self.play(Create(broker_circle))
        
        # Subscribe notifications
        notification = Text(
            "Subscribed!",
            font_size=24, 
            color=BLUE
        )
        notification_arr = VGroup(notification)
        
        self.play(Write(notification_arr))
        
        # Fade out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(broker), 
            FadeOut(topics), 
            FadeOut(notification_arr)
        )


# =============================================================================
# Bridge Architecture
# =============================================================================


class BridgeArchitecture(Scene):
    """Show ESP32-WROOM-32 bridging all platforms."""

    def construct(self):
        # Create title
        title = Text(
            "ESP32 Bridge Architecture",
            font_size=54,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        self.play(Write(title))
        
        # Create nodes
        nodes = VGroup()
        
        # Platform labels
        platform_labels = [
            "daisy_seed",
            "ESP32-WROOM",
            "axoloti",
            "xiao",
            "Cloud MQTT"
        ]
        
        # Create and animate nodes
        node_positions = {
            0: UP,
            1: LEFT,
            2: RIGHT,
            3: DOWN,
            4: UL
        }
        
        for i, label in enumerate(platform_labels):
            node = Text(label, font_size=30, color=WHITE)
            node.next_to(node_positions[i], buff=0.5)
            nodes.add(node)
            
            self.play(Create(node))

        # Create connecting lines
        lines = VGroup(
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[1], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[2], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[3], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[1], nodes[2], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[1], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[2], nodes[3], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[2], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[3], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
        )
        self.play(Create(lines))
        
        # Add legend
        legend = VGroup(
            Text("I2C/PWM", font_size=24),
            Text("BLE Mesh", font_size=24),
            Text("WiFi MQTT", font_size=24),
        )
        
        legend.arrange(UP, buff=0.3).to_corner(DR).scale(0.9)
        self.play(Write(legend))
        
        # Complete animation
        self.wait(3)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(nodes),
            FadeOut(lines),
            FadeOut(legend),
            FadeOut(title)
        )


# =============================================================================
# Full Animation
# =============================================================================


class FullAnimation(Scene):
    """Complete Blender Twin project animation."""

    def construct(self):
        # Title sequence
        title = Text(
            "Blender Twin IoT",
            font_size=60,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        title.to_edge(UP)
        self.play(Write(title))
        
        # Hardware overview
        hardware = Text(
            "ESP32-WROOM-32",
            font_size=40
        )
        self.play(Create(hardware))
        
        # Create nodes
        nodes = VGroup(
            Text("daisy_seed", font_size=40, color=RED),
            Text("ESP32-WROOM", font_size=40, color=BLUE),
            Text("axoloti", font_size=40, color=GREEN),
            Text("xiao", font_size=40, color=YELLOW),
        )
        
        # Position nodes
        nodes[0].to_edge(DL)
        nodes[1].to_edge(DOWN)
        nodes[2].to_edge(DR)
        nodes[3].to_edge(UL)
        
        self.play(Create(nodes[0]))
        self.play(Create(nodes[1]))
        self.play(Create(nodes[2]))
        self.play(Create(nodes[3]))
        
        # Create connections
        lines = VGroup(
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[1], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[2], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[0], nodes[3], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[1], nodes[2], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[1], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[2], nodes[3], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[2], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
            Arrow(nodes[3], nodes[4], buff=0.2),
        )
        
        # Add descriptions
        descriptions = VGroup(
            Text("I2C/PWM", font_size=24, color=BLUE),
            Text("BLE Mesh", font_size=24, color=RED),
            Text("WiFi MQTT", font_size=24, color=GREEN),
            Text("Audio DSP", font_size=24, color=YELLOW),
        )
        
        descriptions.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.play(Create(descriptions))
        
        # Fade out
        self.play(FadeOut(title))
        self.play(FadeOut(nodes))
        self.play(FadeOut(lines))
        self.play(FadeOut(descriptions))


# =============================================================================
# Run
# =============================================================================


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Uncomment to run specific scene:
